# pangolin_virtual_api_key (Resource)

Manages a manual virtual API key (Pangolin 1.26+): a bearer key that lets a client call the public inference resources of the AI gateway. Set either `all_resources` or `resource_ids`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A key limited to one public inference resource, valid for 30 days.
resource "pangolin_virtual_api_key" "ci" {
  name              = "ci"
  description       = "Used by the CI runners"
  resource_ids      = [pangolin_resource.llm.id]
  valid_for_seconds = 2592000
}

# A key for every public inference resource.
resource "pangolin_virtual_api_key" "all" {
  name          = "all"
  all_resources = true
}

output "ci_key" {
  value     = pangolin_virtual_api_key.ci.secret
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the key.

### Optional

- `all_resources` (Boolean) Allow the key on every public inference resource of the organization, including the ones created later. Defaults to `false`.
- `description` (String) A free-text description.
- `resource_ids` (Set of Number) IDs of the public inference `pangolin_resource` the key may call. Required unless `all_resources` is `true`, in which case leave it unset.
- `user_id` (String) ID of an organization member the key is attributed to.
- `valid_for_seconds` (Number) Lifetime of the key in seconds, counted from the apply that sets it. Unset means the key never expires. It cannot be read back, so it is not checked for drift and not set on import.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The virtual API key ID.
- `secret` (String, Sensitive) The key value clients send as a bearer token.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a virtual API key by its ID.
terraform import pangolin_virtual_api_key.ci <virtual_api_key_id>
```
